title: Writesonic Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Free Trial
summary: Writesonic pricing depends on draft volume and feature access. Use the plan comparison to match your actual output without paying for unused features.
body_markdown:
## Moving Writesonic drafts into your tools with Activepieces


It doesn't change what Writesonic costs, but Activepieces, an MIT-licensed automation platform with 747 integrations, moves finished drafts to where your team works and holds them for a human approval first.


That matters because the cheapest Writesonic plan only stays cheap if the handoff work doesn't pile up around it.


In the flow below, one Writesonic draft stops at an approval step with a named reviewer. It then fans out to three places: your CMS (the system that publishes pages), a shared document, and a review channel.


Nothing publishes until the reviewer says so, so the automation never ships an unchecked draft.


Once approved, the draft lands in all three places without anyone copying and pasting.


Activepieces'[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) lists 1 credit per flow run, any number of steps, so the approval step and three deliveries cost one credit, where Zapier's pricing page bills that same run per task and Make's bills it per module.


### Monthly credit allowances by plan


Separate from Writesonic's meter,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) has its own. Per its[pricing page](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , Free includes 1,000 credits a month, Plus includes 10,000, and Team includes 50,000. Plus is ten times Free, and Team is five times Plus.


Before you pick a tier, run one draft through the flow and see how many credits it spends, because credits are the unit to count. Multiply that by your monthly draft count and compare the result to 1,000.


If you land well under it, Free covers you and the upgrade buys nothing. If you land near the ceiling, Plus gives you ten times the room.


Buy for your measured volume, not your hopeful volume; the same discipline applies here as with Writesonic itself. Move up a tier only when a month's real credit use gets close to the cap.


You don't need this at all in two cases. One is a solo writer who pastes each draft into one CMS, since there's no handoff to automate.


The other is a team that already reviews inside Writesonic and publishes from there, since the approval step adds a tool without removing a task.


For everyone else, the question is how many drafts a month need that handoff.
